# Archive entry name used as an extraction path (Java)

`qualor:java/zip-slip` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A01:2021 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Archive extraction that uses the name of an entry, as stored in the archive, in the path of a file
or directory it creates or writes: `ZipEntry.getName()`, `JarEntry.getName()` and Commons
Compress entry names (also a tar entry's link target), reaching file streams and writers,
`File.mkdirs()`, the `Files` methods that write, create, copy, move or link, and Commons IO
writers.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
The archive decides the entry names, and nothing stops a name such as `../../etc/cron.d/x` or an
absolute path. Joining such a name to the extraction directory writes outside it ("zip slip"): an
uploaded archive can overwrite configuration, code or keys and so take over the server.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** each entry is written to the directory joined with its name.

```java
package com.example.unpack;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.zip.ZipEntry;
import java.util.zip.ZipInputStream;

public class Unzipper {
    public static void unzip(Path zip, Path dest) throws IOException {
        try (ZipInputStream in = new ZipInputStream(Files.newInputStream(zip))) {
            ZipEntry entry;
            while ((entry = in.getNextEntry()) != null) {
                Path target = dest.resolve(entry.getName());
                Files.copy(in, target);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the joined path is normalised and the entry is refused unless it stays inside the
directory.

```java
package com.example.unpack;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.zip.ZipEntry;
import java.util.zip.ZipInputStream;

public class Unzipper {
    public static void unzip(Path zip, Path dest) throws IOException {
        try (ZipInputStream in = new ZipInputStream(Files.newInputStream(zip))) {
            ZipEntry entry;
            while ((entry = in.getNextEntry()) != null) {
                Path target = dest.resolve(entry.getName()).normalize();
                if (!target.startsWith(dest)) {
                    throw new IOException("Entry outside the target directory: " + entry.getName());
                }
                Files.copy(in, target);
            }
        }
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Normalise the joined path and skip or refuse the entry unless it still starts with the
  destination: `target.normalize().startsWith(dest)` (with a normalised, absolute `dest`).
- Or compare canonical paths: `file.getCanonicalPath()` must start with the destination's canonical
  path plus `File.separator`.
- Or keep only the last name element (`Path.getFileName()`), or use Commons Compress
  `ArchiveEntry.resolveIn(dest)`.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- `java.util.zip`
- `java.util.jar`
- Apache Commons Compress
- `java.nio.file`
- Apache Commons IO

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Checks that are not recognised, so the code is still reported: ad hoc checks of the name
  (`name.contains("..")`), a check combined with other conditions, a check in a helper method, a
  guard of more than three statements, and the true branch of an `if` that has an `else`.
- A check counts only in these forms: `normalize()` (or `getCanonicalFile().toPath()`) followed by
  `Path.startsWith`, or `getCanonicalPath()` followed by `String.startsWith` of the destination plus
  a separator. `Path.startsWith` without `normalize()`, and `String.startsWith` without a separator,
  are reported, since `dest/../x` and `dest-evil/x` pass them.
- An entry name obtained through a helper method or class is not followed.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
